  # Memory error report host synth-system-channel
section#s1.sec
  ## 1 Summary
  p.grade: hold replacement host synth-system-channel
  p.conclusion: CPU0_B1 S/N 880018: hold replacement (finding, confidence medium). CPU0_B1 and CPU0_B2 share one channel (socket 0 channel 1) and both have errors that are not confined to one place: 181 here, 160 there, between 2026-09-05 and 2026-11-12. Do not pull a DIMM yet. Check the channel first: swap this DIMM with one from another channel and see whether the errors follow it.
  p: 13 more with errors or a finding: CPU0_B2 hold replacement, CPU0_E1 observe, CPU0_F1 observe, CPU0_F2 observe, CPU0_G1 observe, CPU0_H2 observe, CPU1_A1 observe, CPU1_A2 observe, CPU1_C1 observe, CPU1_C2 observe, CPU1_E1 observe, CPU1_G1 observe, CPU1_G2 observe.

The colour and the mark of a stick give the grade of the finding for its DIMM; a red notch on top marks a module with an uncorrected error; a slot without a module is an outline. A stick leads to the finding of its DIMM and shows the details of the module under the pointer.

  p.how: One column per boot, the oldest at the left, and the letter below its number says how it ended: S a fatal hardware error ended it, p another panic, r the boot of the latest scan, - not on record. A cell gives the corrected errors of the boot as a number, U an uncorrected error, X an uncorrected error in a boot that stopped, ? a boot that stopped with no record naming a DIMM, - a DIMM that was not in the host. The table below holds the same.

  p.how: The finding line gives the grade, the rule that set it and what that rule saw. Below stand at most three statements that bear on the decision: what the other rules saw, and checks that speak for the finding ("supports") or against it ("weakens"). A count of records leads to the records. The last line gives the confidence and counts what the whole finding in the appendix adds: further statements, checks that could not be made, missing data.
  ### Rules named in this report
  table.rules
    | rule | grade it gives | fires when
    | R-SOFT-01 | observe | corrected errors without a growing fault: stray errors at places that did not fail again, or a fault that is neither rising nor spreading
    | R-SYS-01 | hold replacement | errors on two or more DIMMs of one channel

  p.how: Each bar splits all errors of the DIMM at one level of its memory: rank, device, bank, row. A segment lies below the segment it belongs to, so the widest path from top to bottom is where the errors are.
  p.how: One bank of one device: rows down, columns across. The shade of a cell is the number of errors in it. A horizontal line is a row fault, a vertical line a column fault, one cell that repeats a single-bit fault, and a cloud over the bank a bank fault. A cell with errors leads to its records.

section#s6.sec
  ## 6 Checks against a wrong diagnosis
  p.how: Each finding was tested against causes outside the DIMM: the slot, the channel, the board, and slot names that disagree between sources. "supports" speaks for the finding and "weakens" against it. An open check could not be made from the records; where a person can settle it, the test is listed below the checks.
  p.sub: 12 more DIMMs have fewer than 10 errors and the finding "observe": their finding is in section 3, and this section leaves them out.
  section#check-dimm-CPU0_B1.dimm
    ### CPU0_B1 hold replacement
    p.hold: A cause outside the DIMM is suspected. Settle that before a DIMM is pulled.
    #### Checks made from the records
    table.checks
      | result | check
      | R-SYS-01 | CPU0_B1 and CPU0_B2 share one channel (socket 0 channel 1) and both have errors that are not confined to one place: 181 here, 160 there, between 2026-09-05 and 2026-11-12 181 records
    #### Tests for a person
    li: Do not pull a DIMM yet. Check the channel first: swap this DIMM with one from another channel and see whether the errors follow it.
  section#check-dimm-CPU0_B2.dimm

section#s7.sec
  ## 7 Data quality
  p.how: What the findings rest on: every source that was looked for, what it yielded, and how much of the location of an error it reports. A finding only says what the observation grade of its records allows.
  ### How the board was drawn
  li: 32 slots on the board, 0 drawn without channels, 0 set aside
  li: the channel count of the processor is not known: the channels of the board could not be checked against it
  li: The population was not checked: the board is not drawn in full.

  ### Records in FMFM field names
  p.how: The error records above with the field names of the FMFM runtime error log, one JSON object per line. A field a source did not report is left out. The lower-case fields are added by MemorY: the observation grade, the source and the place of the original record.
